title: Structure, Dynamics and Free Energy Studies on the Effect of Spot Mutations on SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein Binding with ACE2 Receptor
authors: George Rucker; Hong Qin; Liqun Zhang
one_liner_zh: 该文用全原子MD和FEP研究SARS-CoV-2刺突蛋白RBD突变体与ACE2受体的结合自由能及动态网络，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作和MD方法，但对象非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic continues to infect people worldwide, and the virus continues to evolve in significant ways which can pose challenges to the efficiency of available vaccines and therapeutic drugs and cause future pandemic. Therefore, it is important to investigate the binding and interaction of ACE2 with different RBD variants. A comparative study using all-atom MD simulations was conducted on ACE2 binding with 8 different RBD variants, including N501Y, E484K, P479S, T478I, S477N, N439K, K417N and N501Y-E484K-K417N on RBD. Based on the RMSD, RMSF, and DSSP results, the overall binding of RBD variants with ACE2 is stable, and the secondary structures of RBD and ACE2 are consistent after the spot mutation. Besides that, a similar buried surface area, a consistent binding interface and a similar amount of hydrogen bonds formed between RBD with ACE2 although the exact residue pairs on the binding interface were modified. The change of binding free energy from spot mutation was predicted using the free energy perturbation (FEP) method. It is found that N501Y, N439K, and K417N can strengthen the binding of RBD with ACE2, while E484K and P479S weaken the binding, and S477N and T478I have negligible effect on the binding. Spot mutations modified the dynamic correlation of residues in RBD based on the dihedral angle covariance matrix calculation. Doing dynamic network analysis, a common intrinsic network community extending from the tail of RBD to central, then to the binding interface region was found, which could communicate the dynamics in the binding interface region to the tail thus to the other sections of S protein. The result can supply unique methodology and molecular insight on studying the molecular structure and dynamics of possible future pandemics and design novel drugs.
abstract_zh: 持续的COVID-19疫情继续在全球范围内感染人群，病毒持续以显著方式进化，这可能对现有疫苗和治疗药物的有效性构成挑战，并引发未来大流行。因此，研究ACE2与不同RBD变体的结合及相互作用具有重要意义。本研究采用全原子分子动力学（MD）模拟，对ACE2与8种不同RBD变体（包括RBD上的N501Y、E484K、P479S、T478I、S477N、N439K、K417N及N501Y-E484K-K417N）的结合进行了比较研究。基于RMSD、RMSF和DSSP结果，RBD变体与ACE2的整体结合稳定，且点突变后RBD和ACE2的二级结构保持一致。此外，尽管结合界面上的具体残基对有所改变，但RBD与ACE2之间形成了相似的埋藏表面积、一致的结合界面以及相似数量的氢键。利用自由能微扰（FEP）方法预测了点突变引起的结合自由能变化。研究发现，N501Y、N439K和K417N能增强RBD与ACE2的结合，而E484K和P479S则削弱结合，S477N和T478I对结合影响可忽略不计。基于二面角协方差矩阵计算，点突变改变了RBD中残基的动态相关性。通过动态网络分析，发现了一个从RBD尾部延伸至中心，再到结合界面区域的共同内在网络群落，该群落可能将结合界面区域的动态信息传递至尾部，进而影响S蛋白的其他部分。该结果可为研究未来可能大流行的分子结构和动态提供独特的方法学和分子见解，并有助于设计新型药物。
